clue.text: Stalin remix isn't revolutionary like this

definitions.text: Stalin remix isn't revolutionary like this

indicators.note: revolutionary here means overturned, so the letters of the three words are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A dig at a political mash-up that lacks real revolutionary spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges STALINREMIXISNT; read whole, the clue also describes the creed Stalin professed, which is a revolutionary doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalin's official ideology combined Marx's theory with Lenin's, and it was revolutionary in aim.

clue.text: A thousand ships set out, leading to unfortunate results

indicators.note: set out means the letters are laid out in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Helen's thousand ships set sail, leading to disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The thousand ships recall Helen of Troy's face that launched them.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidents and mishaps are unlucky outcomes.

clue.text: Like ball in rough in game of golf

definitions.meaning: approximate, as with figures given to the nearest ten
one complete circuit of the course, eighteen holes

explanation.surface: A golf ball lost in the long grass during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition, with the second 'in' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means spherical, approximate as in round numbers, and a complete circuit of a golf course.

clue.text: Logical method not excluded on count I'd mishandled

parts.note: not excluded means included, or in

indicators.note: mishandled means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone botches a count but is still included in a logical procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning from particular cases to a general law is the inductive method of logic.

clue.text: Not the finished article? Fine!

indicators.note: not the finished article signals a word left incomplete, missing its final letter

parts.note: an article is a thing, an item

explanation.surface: A grudging verdict that something is not perfect but will do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the finished article' is a stock phrase for something incomplete; here the article, THING, is literally unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine thread or fine hair is slender, so fine can mean narrow and slight.

clue.text: Purpose of certain organs, indeed, seen in power of two

indicators.note: seen in means the word for indeed is placed within the number

parts.note: eight is two cubed, a power of two
yes means indeed, as an affirmation

explanation.surface: A biology lesson on what certain organs are for, with a bit of maths.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyes are the organs whose job is vision.

clue.text: As indicated by control tower, I land in the East

definitions.text: As indicated by control tower, I
definitions.meaning: in the radio alphabet used by air traffic control, the letter I is spoken as this word
the large country in South Asia

explanation.surface: A pilot reporting that they are touching down somewhere in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the NATO code word for the letter I and a country of South Asia.

clue.text: Position of stock often in trouble

definitions.meaning: stock is broth, which goes into a soup

explanation.surface: Shares that are often in a bad way on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' suggests shares; it is broth. 'often' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in difficulties, and literally describes where stock ends up.

clue.text: Time's cut for this book's short version

definitions.text: Time's cut for this book's short version

parts.words: Time's cut for this book's short version
parts.note: cutting the last letter off Time leaves the usual abbreviation of a New Testament epistle's name

explanation.surface: An editor trimming a Time magazine piece for an abridged book.
explanation.walkthrough: TIM, Time cut short, is how this epistle is abbreviated in Bible references.
explanation.definitionFit: Two letters of Paul in the New Testament carry this name, written TIM for short.

clue.text: Healthy small meal that's said to make news briefly

parts.note: sound means healthy, as in sound in wind and limb
a bite is a snack or light meal

explanation.surface: A nutritious snack recommended in a short news report.
explanation.definitionFit: A short quotable phrase spoken for broadcast is exactly a brief remark that makes the news.

clue.text: Cause of current stoppage includes union, in fact

indicators.note: includes signals that one piece is held within the other

parts.note: a dam stops the current of a river
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: A report on a power cut caused by a union strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests electricity and 'stoppage' a strike, but the current is a river's flow, stopped by a DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item of information or given fact is called a datum.

clue.text: Sum up one in front of court as fiend

indicators.note: in front of places the letter for one before the letters for court

parts.note: to sum up is to add
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lawyer summing up before the court, calling someone a fiend.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiend is used informally for an enthusiast or someone hooked, as in a drugs fiend.

clue.text: Part of light inspirational poem turned to expression of grief

indicators.note: turned means the title of the poem is read backwards

parts.note: Kipling's If is a famously inspirational poem
a lament is a song or cry of grief

explanation.surface: A light, uplifting poem that turns into an elegy.
explanation.walkthrough: IF is Rudyard Kipling's poem of advice to a son, often voted Britain's favourite; 'Part of light' means part of a light bulb, not a light poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin glowing wire inside an incandescent bulb is the component that makes the light.

clue.text: Settled on paper facilitating one's vision, naturally

indicators.note: on places the word for settled after the word for paper in this across answer

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
lit, past tense of light, means settled or alighted, as a bird does

explanation.surface: A reader settled with a newspaper that helps them see things naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A place bathed in daylight lets one see by natural light rather than lamps.

clue.text: Trivial matter head doesn't need to be bothered with

definitions.text: head doesn't need to be bothered with
definitions.meaning: something requiring no thought from the brain

explanation.surface: Something so trivial the boss need not be troubled with it.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal term means something so simple that it requires no thought at all.

clue.text: Perhaps Odyssey includes such epic poetry

indicators.note: includes signals that the answer is contained within the run of words

explanation.surface: A literary remark that Homer's Odyssey contains such grand verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece, a rhapsody was a section of epic poetry recited by a performer.

clue.text: Mostly appreciate reform for each person

indicators.note: reform means the remaining letters are formed again in a new order
mostly means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A campaign to reform how everyone is valued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the final E to leave APPRECIAT, which 'reform' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase literally means by heads, so per individual.

clue.text: Bachelor on base welcoming one's fellowship

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: welcoming means the word for base takes in the numeral

parts.note: home is a base, as in baseball
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single man at a military base made to feel part of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured friendliness and camaraderie is the cheerful fellowship of good company.

clue.text: Sailor in front of boat protected by shy youth on board

indicators.note: protected by means the letters for shy wrap around the other pieces

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
taken as written

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of the word boat

explanation.surface: A timid boy hiding behind a sailor at the bow of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text had a stray 'is'; the scan shows none.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy employed to wait on officers and passengers is a young person working aboard a ship.

clue.text: Bobby promises to pay in full

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer, a cop
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A policeman pledging to settle his debts completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something produced in full measure is abundant and plentiful.

clue.text: Support for young boxer, say

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a boxer is a breed of dog, so a young one is a pup

explanation.surface: Encouragement for a fledgling fighter in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' flags that the boxer is an example of a dog, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore something up with a prop is to support it physically or financially.

clue.text: Careful look at country's southern state

parts.note: Peru's, possessive of the South American country
AL is the abbreviation for Alabama, a US southern state

explanation.surface: A close examination of a nation's southern province.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading something through thoroughly is a careful examination of it.

clue.text: Ancient rulers of islands in sound

indicators.note: in sound means the word for the islands is said, giving a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: the Faroes are a group of North Atlantic islands

explanation.surface: Kings who ruled a group of islands across a stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' could be a strait of water around islands; here it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The kings of ancient Egypt bore this title.

clue.text: Crime leaving Canterbury pilgrim penniless

indicators.note: penniless means without P, the abbreviation for a penny

parts.note: the Parson is one of the pilgrims in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales

explanation.surface: A destitute pilgrim on the road from Canterbury turning to crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Old man, one securing large fish

definitions.meaning: a dialect word for an elderly countryman or a boss
someone landing big fish with a hooked pole called a gaff

explanation.surface: An elderly angler hooking a big catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an old fellow or boss, and also, cryptically, one who uses a gaff to land fish.

clue.text: In a good way, one's taken up new language

parts.note: far means to a great degree, as in far better

indicators.note: taken up means the letters are read upwards, backwards in a down answer

parts.note: I's, one is, gives IS

explanation.surface: A learner taking up a new language with great success.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern Persian, the language of Iran, is also called new Persian, a younger form of the ancient tongue.

clue.text: Members you'll find in the gunroom

explanation.surface: Club members gathered in the gunroom of a country house.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both limbs and weapons.

clue.text: Noises from pens and old writing materials

parts.note: inks are materials for writing

explanation.surface: The scratching of pens and old inks in a scriptorium.
explanation.walkthrough: The pens are pigpens, not writing implements.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs make grunting noises, and pigs are kept in pens.

clue.text: Celebration to show appreciation of artist, dividing spoils

indicators.note: dividing means the two pieces split the word for spoils

parts.note: mars means spoils or ruins
dig is slang for to like or appreciate
RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A party in honour of a painter, wrecked by a squabble over loot.
explanation.definitionFit: The carnival on Shrove Tuesday, famous in New Orleans, is a festive celebration.

clue.text: Repressing plan I reformulated, one used to raise game

indicators.note: reformulated means the letters are put together in a new form

explanation.surface: A politician reworking a policy plan to stifle opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: This gundog breed is trained to flush birds from cover for shooting.
